articles.title: Four arrested, 21 assisting MOM investigation into construction-sector "phantom worker" scheme
articles.summary: MOM arrested two company directors and two staff from a construction firm for allegedly making false declarations and collecting kickbacks by creating "phantom workers" to inflate the company's foreign worker quota. A further 21 people are assisting with the investigation.

articles.title: BCA unveils Quantity Surveyors Workgroup recommendations to attract and develop built-environment talent
articles.summary: BCA announced new initiatives to strengthen built environment professions, including recommendations from a Quantity Surveyors Workgroup to attract talent and develop professionals, plus measures to enhance regulatory competency among Qualified Persons, alongside sector excellence awards.

articles.title: Sites in Mandai and Upper Jurong Road to be sold for purpose-built dormitories, over by end-2027
articles.summary: MOM and MND jointly announced that JTC will launch two new purpose-built dormitory sites for tender in the second half of 2027 -- Lorong Lada Hitam 1 in Mandai (10.7ha, about 15,000 beds) and Jurong Apartments at 529 Upper Jurong Road (2ha, about 8,100 beds) -- each on a 30-year lease, as part of a plan to add roughly 71,500 new dormitory beds by the early 2030s to meet employer demand for migrant worker housing.

articles.title: 35-year-old man dies in work-related incident at Jurong Port Road worksite
articles.summary: A 35-year-old worker died after being struck by a hose connected to a compressed-air pump while carrying out foundation works at 37 Jurong Port Road on the evening of 11 September 2026; MOM identified Keller Foundations (S E Asia) Pte Ltd as the worksite's occupier and employer and instructed it to stop all concreting works. It follows an earlier fatal scaffolding collapse on 3 August 2026 at a nearby Jurong Port construction site.

articles.title: BCA commits $112m to R&D and launches Green Mark Version 7
articles.summary: BCA announced $112 million in new Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 funding and launched Green Mark Version 7, a refreshed certification scheme with performance-based pathways aimed at accelerating building decarbonisation.

articles.title: BCA launches Robot Leasing Support Scheme and virtual TOP/CSC inspections
articles.summary: BCA unveiled a Robot Leasing Support Scheme offering up to 50% co-funding for construction robotics, alongside a new whole-of-government virtual inspection process for Temporary Occupation Permit and Certificate of Statutory Completion approvals expected to cut approval times by up to two months.

articles.title: Civils.ai crowned gold winner of inaugural Asia Pacific Construction Startup Competition
articles.summary: ConTech startup Civils.ai won the Gold award at the inaugural Asia Pacific Pitch Day of the Construction Startup Competition, beating four other finalists in the regional contest for construction technology innovation.

articles.title: International Built Environment Week 2026 puts AI at the centre of Singapore's construction industry
articles.summary: International Built Environment Week 2026, held 2-4 September at Marina Bay Sands alongside BEX Asia, focused on AI deployment across design, planning, robotics and building operations, featuring 174 exhibitors including 47 with AI-related offerings.

articles.title: UOL-CapitaLand-SingLand JV wins record $1.43b bid for New Upper Changi Road GLS site
articles.summary: A joint venture of UOL Group, CapitaLand Development and Singapore Land Group won URA's tender for a 99-year leasehold residential site at New Upper Changi Road with a top bid of $1.425 billion ($1,537 psf ppr), a record for Outside Central Region land, beating three other bidders when the tender closed on 1 September 2026.

articles.title: Keppel awarded 50MW data centre capacity for S$1b AI-ready facility on Jurong Island
articles.summary: Keppel was awarded 50MW of new data centre capacity on Jurong Island under Singapore's second Data Centre Call for Application, beating more than 20 other proposals to build the AI-ready Keppel DC SGP 11 facility, with an expected investment of more than S$1 billion and a targeted PUE under 1.2 with over half its power from green energy sources.

articles.title: Changi Airport Group awards contract for new office development at Terminal 3
articles.summary: Changi Airport Group awarded Nakano Singapore a contract to build a six-storey landside office development at Terminal 3, providing about 9,600 sq m of office space across five levels plus a revamped coach stand, to ease capacity constraints as existing T1-T4 landside office space nears its limits. The office block is due for completion in H1 2028 and the coach stand works in H2 2028.

articles.title: MOM to make four heat stress protection measures mandatory for outdoor workers from December 2026
articles.summary: MOM announced that cool drinking water, ice packs, breathable clothing and heat training will become mandatory workplace requirements for outdoor workers, alongside hourly rest breaks when the Wet Bulb Globe Temperature hits 32 degrees C. The measures, which affect construction and other outdoor sectors, take effect from 1 December 2026.

articles.title: Singapore workplace fatalities rise in first half of 2026 as Ministry of Manpower reviews tougher safety measures
articles.summary: MOM reported 21 workplace deaths in Singapore in H1 2026, an annualised fatal injury rate of 1.1 per 100,000 workers, with construction recording 69 fatal and major injuries (a rate of 24.1, the sector's lowest since 2020) even as smaller-scale renovation works saw a slight uptick. The ministry is reviewing a strengthened safety demerit points system and the bizSAFE programme, and has launched a Platform Worker Safety Workgroup alongside an expanded Multi-Agency Taskforce to tackle vehicular risks.

articles.title: Canberra Residences owners sue contractor over unresolved decade-old defects
articles.summary: Canberra Residences' management corporation is suing contractor MCC Engineering, alleging breach of a 2020 settlement meant to fix defects -- including water seepage, ponding and shattered balcony glass -- dating back to the condo's 2013 completion. An 11-day trial is set to begin on 20 October 2026.

articles.title: Wee Hur reports 1HFY2026 earnings of $45.3 mil, up 17.1%; sees recurring income base broaden
articles.summary: Wee Hur Holdings reported 1HFY2026 (ended 30 June) earnings of $45.3 million, up 17.1% year-on-year, on revenue of $163.6 million, driven by a 162.5% surge in construction revenue and a 50.7% jump in workers' dormitory revenue from Pioneer Lodge's ramp-up. The group is broadening its recurring income base via student-accommodation expansion, the upcoming DoubleTree by Hilton Singapore Robertson Quay, and its stake in Wycombe Abbey International School Singapore.

articles.title: Singapore's plans to clear forest for homes lead to rare public protests
articles.summary: HDB's plans to clear about 15 of Maju Forest's 23 hectares and part of Gillman Barracks forest for public housing have drawn unusually vocal opposition, including over 60,000 petition signatures and a rally of more than 2,000 people at Speakers' Corner. The government has since pledged to retain more green space than originally planned, at the cost of fewer homes on both sites.

articles.title: Worker, 23, dies after scaffolding collapse at Jurong Port construction site
articles.summary: A 23-year-old worker died on 3 August 2026 after a formwork structure fell from the fifth storey of a building under construction and struck the lorry he was seated in, at the Jurong Port Integrated Construction and Prefabrication Hub project. Main contractor HPC Builders was instructed to cease all formwork activities as MOM investigates.

articles.title: China's securities regulator balks at bonds that helped property developers restructure debt
articles.summary: China's CSRC has begun declining to register mandatory convertible bonds -- a debt-to-equity tool central to several developers' offshore restructurings -- rejecting Country Garden's filing over its status as a discredited entity and pushing back on Sino-Ocean Group's plans. Bloomberg Intelligence estimates the affected restructurings could have created over 27 billion new shares, adding fresh uncertainty for an industry that has defaulted on roughly $130 billion of debt.

articles.title: Bathla Group faces funding talks as $2.5 billion debt crisis deepens
articles.summary: Insolvent Australian developer Bathla Group secured a temporary funding agreement with five lenders on 7 September 2026, buying two more weeks of survival after standing down about 213 of its 350 staff and halting work at most of its sites, with only 14 continuing; the group carries roughly $3.4 billion in total debt.

articles.title: Bangkok data centres face scrutiny over safety, regulatory gaps
articles.summary: Bangkok's more than 30 data centres are under scrutiny after regulators found some operators classifying their buildings as warehouses to skirt stricter industrial rules, with backup diesel stores as high as 429,000 litres escaping fuel-depot classification under Thailand's 500,000-litre threshold. The Thai government has suspended new standalone data centre projects and formed a Data Centre Business Policy Committee to set unified national standards on safety, energy, water and land use.

articles.title: China's property presale overhaul threatens 30% hit to land sale revenue, Goldman says
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs economists estimate China's shift away from presales toward a completed-homes sales model -- which historically funded roughly 40% of developers' construction capital -- will cut government land sale revenue by 30%, worsening pressure on already-stretched local government finances after land sale revenue fell 30.8% year-on-year in the first seven months of 2026. The overhaul raises the presale threshold to topping out a building's main structure, curbing cash-strapped developers' ability to buy new land.

articles.title: Bathla Group's collapse jolts Australia's private credit lenders
articles.summary: Sydney developer Bathla Group collapsed into voluntary administration owing about A$3.4 billion (A$3.08b to secured lenders), rattling private-credit funds that had financed its projects on promises of roughly 15% annual returns. Administrators have warned that construction on sites whose lenders don't join an emergency funding deal may not be able to continue.

articles.title: CapitaLand Targets $500 Million for Third Asian Credit Fund
articles.summary: CapitaLand Investment is seeking $500 million in investor commitments for its third Asia Pacific credit fund (ACP III), following the $320 million close of its second vehicle in April 2026, continuing a strategy focused on senior secured, asset-backed real estate credit investments.

articles.title: CapitaLand Investment retrenches about 90 employees in Singapore
articles.summary: CapitaLand Investment announced on 3 September 2026 that it is retrenching about 90 employees in Singapore, roughly 4% of its Singapore workforce, as part of a periodic organisational restructuring. The Singapore Industrial and Services Employees' Union said affected staff will receive severance packages, career transition support and counselling.

articles.title: China's property overhaul puts strain on local government income
articles.summary: Beijing scrapped a land auction for a roughly $1.1 billion Jiangtai plot in early September 2026 after only one of three interested developers turned up to bid, days after China's presale-financing overhaul cut area-based land sales 36% week-on-week across 70 major cities; Goldman Sachs projects the reform could cut government land-sale revenue by 30%, straining already-stretched local government finances.

articles.title: BCA partners with Google Maps and Open Government Products to map family- and wheelchair-friendly building features
articles.summary: BCA partnered with Google Maps and Open Government Products to make accessibility information -- such as accessible washrooms, lactation spaces and hearing enhancement systems -- searchable for over 600 Singapore buildings via Google Maps and maps.gov.sg/friendlybuildings, benefiting parents, seniors and persons with disabilities. Coverage is planned to expand to older buildings from early 2027.

articles.title: Asia's data center boom faces backlash
articles.summary: Asia's rapid data centre construction boom is drawing growing community pushback over environmental and health concerns from India to Australia, even as lenders have extended nearly $29 billion in data centre financing since the start of 2026. Overall demand remains strong, but developers are increasingly redirecting investment toward locations with less local opposition rather than slowing expansion.

articles.title: MCST sues developer, four others over alleged defects after concrete piece from condo balcony fell 20m
articles.summary: Foresque Residences' management corporation is suing developer Wincheer Investment and four others -- architect Arc Studio Architecture + Urbanism, structural engineer KTP Consultants, railing engineer GLT Engineers and subcontractor Credence Engineering -- after a cementitious patch detached from a third-floor balcony at Block 105 and fell 20m in February 2025, with hammer-tapping tests later finding about 60% of the block's balcony slab edges producing hollow sounds. The defendants have disputed the allegations and denied liability.

articles.title: Hard rocks, water seepage: LTA flags unexpected construction challenges along North-South Corridor
articles.summary: LTA said tunnelling for the 21.5km North-South Corridor has hit unexpectedly hard rock and mixed ground conditions in Novena and Thomson, plus water seepage weakening the northbound tunnel structure in Novena, forcing smaller section-by-section excavation with extra rock removal, grouting and monitoring. At a briefing on 8 September, LTA said it is still assessing the impact on the project's completion timeline.

articles.title: SingLand gets Written Permission to redevelop Marina Square into Singapore's first hyper-mixed development
articles.summary: SingLand, majority owned by UOL Group, received Written Permission from URA on 31 August 2026 under the Strategic Development Incentive scheme to partially redevelop Marina Square, adding a residential tower, a serviced apartment block and a mixed-use tower designed by PLP Architecture and DP Architects. Marina Square Shopping Mall will close on 31 March 2027 to make way for construction, with the project targeted for completion by 2031.

articles.title: Construction robots on trial could be deployed as early as 2028
articles.summary: JTC and Kajima are trialling autonomous construction machinery -- two excavators and two compactors since January, with autonomous bulldozers and dump trucks to follow in a second phase -- at the Bulim autonomous yard in Jurong Innovation District, aiming to ease manpower constraints and improve worksite safety ahead of a pipeline of at least 800ha of earthworks over the next five years. JTC is targeting deployment at its sites as early as 2028, with the first phase running to early 2027.

articles.title: North-South Corridor: Revised Completion Timeline Due to Complex Engineering Works and Challenging Ground Conditions
articles.summary: LTA announced the 21.5km North-South Corridor will open roughly two years later than planned -- the viaduct section (Admiralty Road West to Lentor Avenue) now from 2029 instead of 2027, and the tunnel section (Lentor Avenue to East Coast Parkway) now from 2031 instead of 2029 -- after harder-than-expected rock at Gambas Avenue/Woodlands Avenue 8 and Thomson, plus fractured rock and groundwater near the operational North-South Line at Novena, required more complex engineering works. LTA said the cost impact of the delay will only be known after the project is completed.

articles.title: Tender award for URA sale site at Lorong Puntong / Sin Ming Avenue
articles.summary: URA awarded the 99-year leasehold residential site at Lorong Puntong / Sin Ming Avenue (Bishan, about 140 units) to Eco World Development (S) Pte Ltd as the highest tenderer, at a bid of $208,099,000 ($17,350.26 per sq m gross floor area). The tender, launched 25 June 2026, closed on 15 September 2026.

articles.title: Singapore Tourism Board launches tender for mixed-use development at historic 37 Emerald Hill
articles.summary: STB launched a Concept and Price Revenue tender on 16 September 2026 for a heritage-sensitive, hotel-led mixed-use redevelopment of 37 Emerald Hill (the former Singapore Chinese Girls' School site, later Chatsworth International School), part of the Orchard Road Rejuvenation Plan. The 1.04ha site permits up to 16,664 sq m GFA on a 50-year lease with a 20-year extension option, and the tender closes 16 March 2027.

articles.title: HDB completes Tengah BTO project using new technologies
articles.summary: HDB said its first Construction Transformation Project, Garden Waterfront II @ Tengah, has achieved a 25% site productivity improvement using technologies including the largest 3D-printed freestanding structure in an HDB development and an intelligent lifting frame developed with NUS and A*STAR that could cut hoisting man-hours by 30%. Garden Waterfront I @ Tengah, the project's second BTO development under the scheme, is due to complete by end-2026.

articles.title: Decisions to consider building homes on greenery or heritage sites not made lightly: Indranee
articles.summary: Second Minister for National Development Indranee Rajah said decisions to develop greenery or heritage sites for housing are made only when no suitable brownfield sites exist, balancing competing land needs against enlarging space via reclamation, taller buildings or going deeper. She was speaking on 14 September ahead of a closed-door youth dialogue on housing, amid ongoing public feedback such as the Maju Forest/Gillman Barracks backlash.

articles.title: Timeline, reclamation profile of new western island not yet determined: Chee Hong Tat
articles.summary: Minister for National Development Chee Hong Tat said in a written parliamentary reply on 8 September that the reclamation profile, land use plans, construction methods and timeline for Singapore's planned new western island have not yet been determined, with feasibility studies, site investigations and engineering/environmental studies still underway.

articles.title: When condo defects emerge years later, who pays?
articles.summary: A Straits Times explainer on Singapore condo-defect disputes -- citing the Canberra Residences and Foresque Residences lawsuits -- notes developers often wind up project-specific companies after completion, leaving management corporations with no one to sue, while a latent-defect claim in tort is subject to a 15-year long-stop limitation period.

articles.title: URA to review guidelines on floor space to give developers more design flexibility: Chee Hong Tat
articles.summary: Minister for National Development Chee Hong Tat announced at the Singapore Corporate Awards on 21 September that URA is reviewing gross floor area (GFA) guidelines to give developers more design flexibility and encourage heat-resilience and thermal-comfort features, and that BCA will let reinforcement steel be tested earlier in production by accredited labs, potentially cutting testing workload and cost by up to 90%. He also announced a new Job Redesign Initiative for Decarbonisation, run with BCA, SCCCI and the Singapore Contractors Association, to help built-environment firms upskill staff in sustainable construction and carbon accounting; 15 companies have already joined.
